en:As cities become more crowded, planners look for ways to provide green space close to where people live. Large parks offer room for sport and long walks, but land in city centres can be expensive. Some communities therefore create small parks on unused plots. These spaces may contain just a few trees, benches, and a short path. Their size limits the activities they can support, but a nearby place to sit outside can still be valuable to local residents.

en:Good design starts by asking how the space will be used. Older residents may need comfortable seating and shade. Families may want a safe place for children, while office workers may visit only during a lunch break. A design that meets one group’s needs may not meet another’s. Planners should also consider maintenance. Trees and paths require care, and this work continues after the opening day. A park that looks attractive in a drawing will not remain useful if nobody maintains it. There is no single design that works in every neighbourhood. The purpose of a small park should guide the decisions about its layout and long-term care.
en:A small park should meet local people’s needs. It also needs long-term care. Trees and paths must be maintained after the park opens.
en:Families may need a play area, while older residents may need shade.
